questions.stem: A bulk transfer improves after switching to BBR, while the SYN/SYN-ACK still negotiate window scaling. Which mechanism changed?
options: The receiver's advertised window ceiling
The firewall policy's traffic shaper
The sender's congestion-control model
The TCP MSS advertised by the client
feedback: Window scaling is negotiated in the handshake and is independent of the congestion algorithm.
A shaper controls rate; it was held constant in this comparison.
Correct: BBR changes congestion-control behavior using bottleneck bandwidth and RTT estimates.
MSS controls segment size, not the congestion-control model.

questions.stem: A proxied download stalls near a small receive-window limit. The capture shows no window-scale option in the handshake. What should be investigated first?
options: TCP option handling and endpoint window scaling
The FortiGate BBR/CUBIC selection
The SD-WAN member health-check threshold
The server's TLS certificate chain
feedback: Correct: missing window scaling can cap the usable TCP receive window; it is not a BBR diagnosis.
Changing BBR cannot restore a missing window-scale negotiation.
SD-WAN health checks do not explain a negotiated TCP receive-window ceiling.
TLS trust affects session establishment, not the TCP receive-window option.

questions.stem: Which statement is accurate about the FortiOS 8.0 congestion-control setting?
options: It is configured independently on each firewall policy
It changes TCP window scaling for all clients
It selects an algorithm only for UDP flows
It is a system-global CUBIC/BBR choice
feedback: The setting is global rather than a per-policy control.
Window scaling remains a separate TCP handshake option.
UDP has no TCP congestion-control algorithm selection.
Correct: FortiOS exposes a system-global choice between CUBIC and BBR.

questions.stem: A BBR test has high retransmissions and the same poor throughput as CUBIC. Which next action is most defensible?
options: Increase the BBR interval until loss disappears
Find the loss or queueing source on the path
Disable TCP window scaling on both endpoints
Move the flow to an unrelated SD-WAN zone
feedback: There is no BBR interval that repairs a lossy physical path.
Correct: congestion control cannot create capacity or repair drops; identify the loss source.
Disabling window scaling would reduce the receive window and can worsen throughput.
Changing zones without evidence alters the path and invalidates the comparison.

questions.stem: A controlled A/B test is being prepared for CUBIC versus BBR. Which test design best isolates the algorithm?
options: Change MTU and shaper during each run
Use different servers and transfer sizes
Keep endpoints, path, load and duration constant
Compare one idle run with one busy run
feedback: Changing MTU and shaping introduces confounding variables.
Different servers and file sizes make throughput comparisons unreliable.
Correct: keep the path and workload fixed so the congestion-control selection is the variable.
Different congestion levels prevent attributing the result to the algorithm.

questions.stem: FortiManager and a FortiSASE instance are registered under the same FortiCare account. What is required for onboarding?
options: A FortiManager Key generated in a separate tenant
The FortiManager Key can be left blank
A dedicated FortiManager ADOM per tunnel
A shared SAML signing certificate between tenants
feedback: A key is not required when both products share the same FortiCare account.
Correct: the documented same-account case permits the FortiManager Key field to remain blank.
ADOM placement is an administrative choice, not a tunnel prerequisite.
SAML signing certificates are not the FortiManager-to-SASE management association key.

questions.stem: A SASE instance is under a different FortiCare account but the same FortiCloud child-OU tree. Which onboarding step applies?
options: Move both products into one ADOM first
Use the old Fabric View connector
Generate a FortiManager Key in SASE Central Management Settings
Create a second FortiManager appliance for the tenant
feedback: ADOM grouping does not establish the account/OU association.
The FortiSASE Connector was removed from Fabric View in this workflow.
Correct: a key is generated when accounts differ but remain in the same OU hierarchy.
Multiple SASE instances can be managed by one FortiManager when prerequisites are met.

questions.stem: Three isolated FortiSASE instances appear under one FortiManager ADOM. What does that prove?
options: They are separate managed-device objects in one administrative group
Their user databases and security PoPs are merged
Traffic can pass between the three tenant networks
One FortiCare account owns all three SASE licenses
feedback: Correct: ADOM membership groups management objects; it does not merge SASE tenants.
FortiSASE instances remain isolated environments.
ADOM membership does not create data-plane connectivity.
The architecture guide describes one FortiSASE instance per FortiCare account.

questions.stem: A FortiSASE device cannot be added and the FortiManager Key is valid. Which prerequisite should be checked next?
options: The FortiGate BGP router ID
The FortiAnalyzer SIEM database
The SASE tenant's Central Management enablement
The switch auto-network management VLAN
feedback: A BGP router ID is unrelated to SASE management onboarding.
FortiAnalyzer's database does not authorize the FortiSASE device.
Correct: Central Management must be enabled; select availability may require Support enablement.
FortiSwitch native VLAN settings do not control FortiSASE registration.

questions.stem: A FortiData Risk Record is visible in Log Browse and Logs > All, but no Event Monitor alert exists. What is missing?
options: The FortiData device registration
The raw Xlog transport path
The SIEM database insertion
A custom event handler for Risk Record logs
feedback: Registration is already evidenced by the received/queryable record.
Raw transport is already evidenced by Log Browse.
Database insertion is already evidenced by Logs > All.
Correct: the default handler triggers Issue logs; Risk Record needs a custom handler.

questions.stem: A FortiData Xlog file appears in Log Browse but the same incident cannot be found in Logs > All. Which stage needs investigation?
options: SIEM database insertion and parsing
The Event Monitor notification email
The FortiSASE tenant key
The endpoint's RADIUS survivability cache
feedback: Correct: raw receipt is proven; the next stage is insertion into siemdb.
Event Monitor is downstream of SIEM insertion and handler evaluation.
FortiSASE tenant keys are unrelated to FortiAnalyzer ingestion.
RADIUS cache is unrelated to FortiData Xlog processing.

questions.stem: Which FortiData incident type is covered by the predefined Ingested External Alerts handler by default?
options: Risk Record only
Issue logs
Integration Event only
All three types without configuration
feedback: Risk Record is supported for ingestion but requires a custom handler for alerting.
Correct: the predefined handler is enabled by default for Issue logs.
Integration Event requires a custom event handler for alerting.
The three types are supported in the database, but default alert mapping is narrower.

questions.stem: What does a FortiData record in Logs > All prove that a raw file in Log Browse does not?
options: The FortiData license is current
An Event Monitor alert has been created
The record has been inserted into siemdb
A custom handler exists for every incident type
feedback: License state is a separate entitlement check.
An alert is a downstream event-handler result.
Correct: Logs > All is the SIEM database query view.
A database record does not prove a custom handler is configured.

questions.stem: A port cannot be added to a manual trunk. The generated trunk shows auto-isl 1 and includes that port. What is the likely cause?
options: Auto-topology currently owns the port
The port has an invalid STP edge setting
The switch lacks a FortiManager ADOM
The port has no LLDP neighbor information
feedback: Correct: auto-ISL owns discovered peer links and can prevent manual trunk membership.
STP edge is a generated ISL property, not the ownership cause.
FortiManager ADOM membership is unrelated to switch trunk membership.
Auto-topology uses peer discovery; an active generated trunk is already visible.

questions.stem: Which design check is explicitly required when selecting the auto-network mgmt-vlan?
options: It must match the FortiGate's WAN VLAN
It must be the same as the default SVI
It must not reuse an existing SVI VLAN
It must be outside the allowed VLAN range
feedback: The guide does not require a WAN VLAN match.
The guide explicitly warns against using the same VLAN for mgmt-vlan and an SVI.
Correct: avoid a duplicate management VLAN/SVI identity.
The allowed VLAN range for the ISL is 1 through 4094.

questions.stem: A standalone FortiSwitch was factory-reset and unexpectedly formed an ISL. Which explanation fits the documented defaults?
options: Factory reset disables auto-network
Auto-topology is enabled after factory reset
Only FortiManager can create ISL trunks
ISL formation requires manual LACP mode
feedback: The documented default is enabled, not disabled.
Correct: auto-network is enabled after factory reset in standalone mode.
Auto-topology can create the ISL locally without FortiManager.
The generated ISL uses LACP-active automatically.

questions.stem: Which attribute set describes the generated auto-ISL switch interface?
options: Native VLAN 1, DHCP snooping untrusted, STP edge enabled
LACP passive, VLANs 10-100, STP edge enabled
Manual LACP, routed-only VLANs, DHCP snooping disabled
LACP-active, allowed VLANs 1-4094, DHCP snooping trusted
feedback: The native VLAN is determined by mgmt-vlan, not always VLAN 1.
The generated trunk is LACP-active and STP edge is disabled.
The interface is an ISL with a defined VLAN list, not routed-only.
Correct: these are documented generated-ISL properties.

questions.stem: RADIUS is unreachable. An employee's previously authenticated station reconnects, but a new laptop cannot join. What explains the difference?
options: The new laptop is on the wrong AP radio
The old station bypassed all SSID policy
Only previously authenticated clients have cached credentials
The new laptop must use a different VLAN
feedback: The scenario does not establish a radio problem.
Survivability does not bypass all SSID policy.
Correct: the local cache supports previously authenticated stations, not first-time authentication.
A VLAN change does not create a missing authentication cache entry.

questions.stem: For EAP-PEAP survivability, which RADIUS response detail is required by the guide?
options: Fortinet-AS-Credential-Hash or Cisco-AVPair AS-Credential-Hash
A DHCP Option 82 remote-ID with the AP serial
A BGP community that identifies the SSID
An IPsec VPN-ID carrying the wireless VRF
feedback: Correct: the credential-hash attribute is required for the documented PEAP cache behavior.
DHCP relay metadata does not provide the PEAP credential hash.
BGP communities do not populate the wireless survivability cache.
VPN-ID/IPIP is an SD-WAN segmentation mechanism.

questions.stem: A cached station remains online after a direct RADIUS test fails. Which interpretation is correct?
options: The RADIUS server has recovered fully
The test command proves the cache is empty
The SSID has switched to open authentication
The station may be using its local survivability entry
feedback: The direct test failed, so server recovery is not proven.
The cache must be inspected separately.
Survivability does not convert the SSID to open authentication.
Correct: the client and direct test exercise different authentication paths.

questions.stem: The station's cache entry has expired. What should happen during a continued RADIUS outage?
options: It receives unlimited cached authorization
It is no longer authorized by the fallback
It is moved automatically to the guest VLAN
It becomes a local RADIUS server for peers
feedback: The interval is bounded; authorization is not unlimited.
Correct: after the configured interval expires, the cached station is no longer authorized.
The guide does not describe an automatic guest-VLAN transition.
A wireless client never becomes the RADIUS server through this feature.

questions.stem: A switch-side description changes, but FortiNAC keeps its old label after routine polling. Which setting explains this behavior?
options: Preserve Port Names remains enabled
The switch has no IP address
The RADIUS accounting port is blocked
The FortiNAC server has no SAML certificate
feedback: Correct: preservation is enabled by default and keeps FortiNAC's label authoritative.
The scenario concerns an already modeled switch interface.
RADIUS accounting is unrelated to port-description synchronization.
SAML certificates do not control switch interface labels.

questions.stem: The operator wants switch descriptions to replace FortiNAC labels. Which action matches the documented behavior?
options: Restart only the switch's RADIUS process
Run L2 polling repeatedly without changing settings
Disable Preserve Port Names at the intended scope, then resync
Delete every port group before the next poll
feedback: The RADIUS process does not control interface description refresh.
Routine L2 polling is not the documented description-overwrite trigger.
Correct: disable preservation globally or per device and run Resync Interfaces.
Deleting port groups is unnecessary and risks losing operational grouping.

questions.stem: A chassis module is inserted and FortiNAC re-indexes interfaces. What secondary effect should be checked?
options: The FortiSASE invitation code
The BBR congestion algorithm
The FortiAuthenticator license timer
Manual port-group associations on recreated interface models
feedback: Endpoint enrollment codes are unrelated to switch model indexing.
TCP congestion control is unrelated to FortiNAC interface models.
VM license validation is unrelated to chassis interface indexing.
Correct: re-indexing may delete/recreate interface models and affect manual groups.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes L2 polling from Resync Interfaces?
options: Both operations always rebuild the full interface model
L2 polling learns state/MAC/VLAN; resync refreshes interface model data
Resync Interfaces only validates RADIUS shared secrets
L2 polling updates all port descriptions regardless of preservation
feedback: The operations have different scope; they are not interchangeable.
Correct: L2 polling is state-oriented; resync reads interface information and descriptions under the configured preservation behavior.
RADIUS shared secrets are not the purpose of interface resync.
Port-description updates depend on Preserve Port Names and resync/service restart.

questions.stem: A cloud-managed switch exposes RADIUS but no SNMP or CLI. Which FortiNAC-F release first supports the documented RADIUS-only model?
feedback: The guide specifies 7.6.7 and later.
The documented minimum is not 7.6.5.
Correct: RADIUS-only device support is available in FortiNAC-F 7.6.7+.
7.2.2 predates the feature.

questions.stem: A RADIUS response must include VLAN-specific attributes and RFC5176 CoA behavior. Which object should be checked?
options: The SSO Address Group
The Response Attribute Configuration
The switch's SNMP read community
The FortiGate auto-ISL trunk
feedback: SSO address groups are used for SSO/VPN configuration, not RADIUS response attributes.
Correct: Response Attribute Configurations define returned attributes and RFC5176 mode.
RADIUS-only devices do not require SNMP management credentials.
Auto-ISL is unrelated to FortiNAC RADIUS response construction.

questions.stem: The Device Migration page shows Legacy Mode as N/A for a RADIUS-only device. What does that mean?
options: The device cannot be placed in selector mode
The device has no RADIUS server configured
The device must be moved to global legacy mode
The device does not support legacy mode
feedback: N/A does not mean selector mode is unavailable.
RADIUS configuration must still be checked separately.
Global legacy mode is a system migration state, not a device requirement.
Correct: RADIUS-only devices cannot enable the legacy device-bound mode.

questions.stem: An administrator wants to test one migrated device. Which action should occur before disabling Global Legacy Mode?
options: Create/review selectors and test devices individually
Disable Global Legacy Mode, then build selectors
Delete all legacy model configurations immediately
Turn on legacy mode for every RADIUS-only device
feedback: Correct: migrate and test devices individually; disable the global control only after all required selectors are ready.
The guide warns the global action is irreversible and removes the migration wizard.
Deleting model configuration before selector creation can lose device-bound configuration.
RADIUS-only devices cannot enable legacy mode.

questions.stem: Two selectors match the same device, one specific and one broad. What is the safest design?
options: Put the broad selector above all specific rules
Disable every selector except the broad rule
Rely on alphabetical selector-name order
Rank the specific selector ahead of the broad match
feedback: A broad rule can capture traffic before the intended specific rule.
Disabling all specific rules defeats the reusable selector model.
The guide uses selector rank/conditions, not alphabetical names.
Correct: ensure the specific rule wins before a broad catch-all.

questions.stem: The FortiAuthenticator GUI works, but RADIUS and SAML authentication stop after a long Internet outage. What should be checked first?
options: The AP's survivability cache
The FortiManager ADOM lock
The subscription license's FDN validation state
The FortiSwitch auto-network mgmt-vlan
feedback: Wireless cache state does not explain platform-wide authentication service shutdown.
ADOM locks do not control FortiAuthenticator licensing.
Correct: loss of update.fortiguard.net validation for 30 days disables the subscription license and halts authentication.
The switch management VLAN is unrelated to VM subscription validation.

questions.stem: How should subscription licensing be handled in an active/passive FortiAuthenticator HA pair?
options: Install separate subscription files on both nodes
Use one perpetual license on the active node only
Mix perpetual active with subscription passive
Copy the active license file to every unrelated VM
feedback: Correct: each HA member requires its own subscription VM license file.
The guide says mixing perpetual and subscription licenses in one pair is unsupported.
A mixed licensing model is explicitly unsupported.
Licensing is per HA member, not a license shared with unrelated VMs.

questions.stem: Which command reports subscription entitlement information fetched from FortiGuard/FDN?
options: get system license-info
diagnose system updated info
diagnose system updated status
diagnose debug application radiusd 3
feedback: This shows local license information rather than FDN-fetched status.
This displays runtime update information.
Correct: the documented command displays license information fetched from FDN.
The documented update daemon debug command is not a radiusd command.

questions.stem: A 6.6.7 VM must be upgraded and a subscription license is available. What is the safe prerequisite?
options: Apply the 8.0 subscription license before any upgrade
Upgrade to FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0 or later first
Mix a perpetual license on the active node
Disable FDN validation for the migration window
feedback: The subscription VM license requires 8.0.0 or later.
Correct: upgrade to a supported release before applying the subscription license.
Mixing license types in HA is unsupported.
The feature requires FDN validation; disabling it is not the documented migration path.

questions.stem: A user is logged into FortiPAM but cannot open a secret until re-authenticating. Which control is responsible?
options: Access Authentication on the secret policy
The target's password changer interval
The SSH filter profile only
The FortiPAM ADOM assignment
feedback: Correct: Access Authentication is a separate step-up gate at secret access/launch time.
Password changing manages credentials, not user step-up authentication.
SSH filtering blocks commands after launch; it does not gate secret viewing.
ADOM is not the FortiPAM secret-access control in this workflow.

questions.stem: A policy needs immediate-use re-authentication with no long access window. Which duration is documented for that behavior?
options: 60 minutes
180 minutes
0 minutes
30 minutes
feedback: 60 minutes is the documented default, not immediate-use duration.
180 minutes is the upper end of the documented range.
Correct: zero indicates short-lived authentication for immediate use.
Thirty minutes is a possible configured duration, not the special zero value.

questions.stem: A user signed in through remote RADIUS/LDAP reaches the Access Authentication dialog. Which documented option applies?
options: Authenticate using the target's SSH key
Authenticate using FortiPAM login credentials
Reuse the last approval decision
Skip the step-up check automatically
feedback: The target's SSH key is a target credential, not the FortiPAM step-up credential.
Correct: remote RADIUS/LDAP users can select PAM login credentials for this authentication step.
Approval is a separate workflow and does not satisfy re-authentication.
The feature requires authentication; it does not silently skip the check.

questions.stem: A folder policy enables Access Authentication, but one secret opens without a prompt. What should be inspected?
options: The target's default gateway
The global FortiPAM NTP server
The session recording video
The secret-level Session Security override
feedback: The target gateway affects reachability, not policy inheritance.
NTP may affect time-based tokens but is not the first inheritance check.
Recording is a separate session security control.
Correct: the secret can override the folder policy's Access Authentication setting.

questions.stem: An investigation graph connects an incident to a host and user. What does the edge establish by itself?
options: A proven causal chain from user to host
A navigable relationship in FortiSIEM context
That both entities share the same process
That the incident is a confirmed true positive
feedback: Graph proximity does not prove causality.
Correct: the graph organizes identified incident/entity relationships for investigation.
The edge does not prove a shared process without event evidence.
Incident resolution still requires analyst evidence and classification.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to see how related incidents unfolded over time. Which workspace function is most useful?
options: The Timeline panel with ordered playback
The FortiAuthenticator license view
The FortiSwitch auto-ISL status icon
The SASE invitation-code page
feedback: Correct: timeline ordering and playback show when incidents occurred in the selected window.
Licensing is unrelated to incident chronology.
The switch icon is unrelated to SIEM investigation.
Invitation codes are unrelated to incident chronology.

questions.stem: A host node is selected and the analyst needs device context and further related incidents. What is the next step?
options: Clear the root incident immediately
Change the incident severity without evidence
Open entity details/context and expand related objects
Delete the host from the CMDB
feedback: Clearing before reviewing evidence can destroy the investigation trail.
Severity changes do not provide entity context.
Correct: inspect the node sidebar/context and selectively add related entities/incidents.
Deleting the CMDB entity removes useful context rather than investigating it.

questions.stem: A backend PostgreSQL query confirms an incident row exists, but the workspace graph differs. What is the best interpretation?
options: The graph is always identical to raw SQL output
The incident must be a false positive
The SQL result proves every graph edge
Compare scope, time window and relationship expansion
feedback: The graph adds context and relationship logic beyond a raw row query.
Database existence does not classify the incident as false positive.
A row query does not prove the graph's full relationship logic.
Correct: compare filters, time range, organization scope and expansion choices.

questions.stem: Authenticated onboarding is not visible in the FortiSASE portal. What prerequisite may be missing?
options: A FortiSwitch auto-ISL configuration
A FortiManager ADOM lock
A FortiAuthenticator subscription file
Fortinet Support enablement for select availability
feedback: Switch topology is unrelated to SASE onboarding enablement.
An ADOM lock does not expose the SASE feature.
FortiAuthenticator licensing does not enable the SASE feature.
Correct: authenticated onboarding is select availability and may require Support enablement.

questions.stem: After authenticated onboarding is enabled, an endpoint still uses its old invitation code. What is expected?
options: The old code remains valid indefinitely
The new code replaces the old registration code
The endpoint bypasses SAML automatically
The endpoint is converted to a FortiNAC host
feedback: The feature rotates the invitation code; old codes are no longer valid for new registration.
Correct: onboarding generates a new code that must be distributed to endpoints/installers.
SAML authentication is the new gate, not an automatic bypass.
FortiNAC is a separate product and is not the migration target.

questions.stem: An Entra ID user belongs to more than 150 groups. What should be checked in the SAML assertion?
options: The asserted group count and scoped group claim
The FortiGate BBR algorithm
The FortiSwitch native VLAN
The FortiPAM secret checkout duration
feedback: Correct: the guide documents a 150-group assertion limit; scope claims to required groups.
TCP congestion control does not affect SAML group assertions.
Switch VLAN configuration is unrelated to SAML claims.
Secret checkout is a FortiPAM control.

questions.stem: A previously enrolled endpoint fails after authenticated onboarding rollout. Which migration item is most likely stale?
options: Its local DHCP lease timer
The FortiAnalyzer event handler
The EMM installer invitation code
The FortiSIEM graph layout
feedback: A DHCP lease is not the endpoint registration invitation code.
FortiAnalyzer handlers do not update endpoint installers.
Correct: EMM-distributed installers must be updated with the current invitation code/configuration.
Graph layout is unrelated to endpoint onboarding.

questions.stem: Two tenants share one IPsec overlay but use separate VRFs. Which encapsulation preserves VRF identity through the tunnel?
options: GRE over UDP without a VPN ID
A single global route table for both tenants
VPN-ID/IPIP encapsulation
A shared DHCP relay identifier
feedback: The documented segmentation feature uses VPN-ID/IPIP, not generic GRE.
A single route table removes the required VRF separation.
Correct: VPN-ID/IPIP carries the VRF identity through the shared tunnel.
DHCP relay identifiers do not carry VRF identity in the IPsec overlay.

questions.stem: VRF-A at spoke 1 must reach VRF-A at spoke 2 but never VRF-B. What should the design enforce?
options: Consistent VRF identity and per-VRF route exchange
A shared default route imported into every VRF
A route leak between all tenant VRFs
One tunnel interface address reused as every loopback
feedback: Correct: consistent VRF IDs and route policy preserve same-VRF reachability and cross-VRF isolation.
A shared default route can create unintended cross-tenant reachability.
Unrestricted route leaking defeats the isolation requirement.
Loopback IPv6 exchange is separate from reusing one address for all tenants.

questions.stem: A health check traverses a multi-VRF tunnel but reaches the wrong tenant's server. Which setting should be reviewed?
options: The FortiPAM Access Authentication duration
The FortiGate global BBR selection
The FortiSwitch auto-network mgmt-vlan
The health check's VRF and source address
feedback: Secret access duration is unrelated to SD-WAN probes.
TCP congestion control does not select the health-check VRF.
The switch management VLAN is unrelated to the routed overlay probe.
Correct: set the health-check VRF and source so the hub forwards it in the same VRF.

questions.stem: A FortiGate itself cannot source a local-out probe through the VPN-ID/IPIP segmented overlay. What limitation applies?
options: VPN-ID/IPIP is supported only for local-out traffic
The feature applies to forwarded traffic, not local-out traffic
IPv6 segmentation requires a separate tunnel per tenant
BGP must be disabled on all spokes
feedback: The guide states the opposite: local-out traffic is not supported by this encapsulation.
Correct: the documented VPN-ID/IPIP segmentation applies to forwarding traffic only.
The design is specifically intended to share one overlay across VRFs.
BGP route exchange is part of the multi-VRF design.
